📊 About CTR Decline in Digital Advertising
CTR naturally decreases over time for all creatives — this is normal audience saturation and banner blindness. What distinguishes creatives is how fast and how far CTR drops. The normalized view (% of launch-week baseline) makes this immediately comparable: top performers retain ~33% of launch CTR, stable creatives ~23%, and fatigued ones only ~16%.

🔮 Predict a New Creative

Configure a hypothetical creative and get an instant performance estimate based on patterns learnt from all 1 080 existing creatives. The model uses K-Means cluster matching + PCA feature profiles.

How it works

The predictor uses patterns from the full 1 080-creative dataset to estimate performance of an untested configuration.

① Cluster matching
Finds which of the 8 K-Means clusters your creative profile resembles most, based on format, vertical, theme and tone.
② Feature adjustments
Applies boosts and penalties from the Random Forest feature importance for your specific KPI goal.
③ Similar creatives
Surfaces the top 3 existing creatives with the closest profile to benchmark your estimate.
⚠ Limitations
This is a heuristic estimate. Re-run ml_pipeline_sklearn.py locally to embed full PCA inference (sklearn model parameters) for higher accuracy.

📖 Help & Metric Glossary

Everything you need to interpret the dashboard. Use the 💬 Ask Claude button (bottom-right) to ask follow-up questions in plain English.

📊 Performance Metrics

CTR — Click-Through Rate
Clicks ÷ Impressions. Fraction of users who tap on the ad after seeing it.
Typical: 0.8–2.5%  |  Strong: >2%
CVR — Conversion Rate
Conversions ÷ Clicks. Fraction of people who clicked and then completed the goal action (install, purchase, signup, booking…).
Typical: 10–40%
ROAS — Return on Ad Spend
Revenue ÷ Spend. For every $1 spent on this ad, how many dollars of attributed revenue were generated.
>1.0 = profitable  |  >2.0 = strong
IPM — Installs per Mille
Conversions per 1 000 impressions. Direct efficiency measure for install or acquisition campaigns.
Typical: 3–15
perf_score
Composite performance score (0–1) derived from CTR, CVR, ROAS, and IPM normalised within the full dataset. 1.0 = the strongest creative; 0 = the weakest.
>0.65 = top performer  |  <0.35 = underperformer

📉 Fatigue & Decay

first_7d_ctr
Average CTR across the first 7 active days. This is the "freshness baseline" — how the ad performed when audiences were still seeing it for the first time.
last_7d_ctr
Average CTR across the most recent 7 days of data.
ctr_decay_pct
(last_7d_ctr − first_7d_ctr) / first_7d_ctr. How much CTR has dropped relative to launch. Always negative for real ads. −0.67 means CTR dropped 67%.
cvr_decay_pct
Same as ctr_decay_pct but for Conversion Rate.
fatigue_day
The day number (since launch) when performance decay first became material. If blank, no significant fatigue was detected.
CTR retention (normalized view)
last_7d_ctr ÷ first_7d_ctr, shown as 100% at launch. All digital ads decline — the question is how much is retained. Top performers keep ~33% of launch CTR; fatigued ads only ~16%.

🎨 Creative Attributes

text_density
Fraction of the visual area covered by text. High values mean text-heavy ads; low values mean image-dominant.
0 (minimal) → 1 (text-heavy)
readability_score
Estimated ease of reading the copy. Higher = clearer, simpler language.
0 → 1 (higher = easier to read)
brand_visibility_score
How prominently the brand logo or name appears in the creative.
0 → 1
clutter_score
How visually busy or crowded the layout is. High clutter reduces attention and recall.
0 (clean) → 1 (cluttered)
novelty_score
Estimated originality relative to the other creatives. Novel creatives stand out more and avoid banner blindness.
0 → 1
motion_score
Intensity of movement or animation in the ad. Relevant for video and playable formats.
0 (static) → 1 (high motion)
duration_sec
Length of the video or interactive experience in seconds. Static images = 0.
has_gameplay
1 if the creative shows actual gameplay footage. Strongly predictive for CPA and IPM campaigns.
has_ugc_style
1 if the creative mimics user-generated content (creator-style, selfie format, etc.). Tends to increase authenticity perception and CTR.
has_price / has_discount_badge
1 if a price or a sale/bonus badge is visible. Price signals drive conversion intent; discount badges create urgency.

🏷 Status Labels

top_performer
High performance across primary KPI metrics, and CTR holds well over time. Action: Scale budget and create A/B variants.
stable
Solid and consistent, but not exceptional. No strong fatigue signal detected. Action: Monitor and consider iterating on the concept.
fatigued
Clear performance decay detected past fatigue_day. Audiences have seen the ad too many times. Action: Pause or refresh. Do not increase spend.
underperformer
Consistently weak primary KPI from launch. No evidence of a strong period. Action: Reallocate budget. Retire or fundamentally rethink the creative.

🎯 KPI Goals

CPA — Cost per Acquisition
The campaign is optimising to minimise cost per conversion (install, purchase, signup). The most relevant metric is CVR — the higher, the fewer clicks wasted.
ROAS — Return on Ad Spend
The campaign is optimising for revenue attributed to conversions. The most relevant metric is ROAS — revenue ÷ spend. Must be >1 to be profitable.
IPM — Installs per Mille
The campaign is optimising for install volume relative to impressions. The most relevant metric is IPM — installs per 1 000 impressions.
CTR — Click-Through Rate
The campaign is optimising for engagement — clicks on the ad. The most relevant metric is CTR — clicks ÷ impressions.

🤖 ML Concepts

Feature Importance
How much each creative attribute contributed to the model's predictions. Computed by the Random Forest (average impurity reduction) or XGBoost (gain-based). Values range 0–1 and sum to 1 across all features.
SHAP value
Shapley Additive exPlanation. For a specific creative, the exact contribution of each feature to its predicted score relative to the dataset average. Positive = pushed score up; negative = pulled it down. Used to power the 🤖 Explain button.
PCA (Principal Components)
A mathematical technique that compresses 36 creative features into 20 orthogonal components that capture 93% of the variation in the data. Used for clustering and the Portfolio Optimizer.
K-Means Cluster
One of 8 creative archetypes identified by grouping similar creatives together. Creatives in the same cluster share similar format, theme, tone, and typically similar performance profiles.
R² (Cross-Validation)
How well the model predicts performance on creatives it has not been trained on. R² = 1.0 is perfect; R² = 0 means no better than always predicting the average. Values above 0.6 are considered good.
Orthogonality Score
In the Portfolio Optimizer: the fraction of a creative's PCA feature vector that lies outside the subspace already covered by your portfolio (computed via Gram-Schmidt). 100% = completely unexplored creative territory.

🗺 Tab-by-Tab Quick Guide

🔍 Performance Explorer
Filter by KPI, status, format or vertical. Click a creative card to open the detail modal. Click 🤖 Explain to get a plain-English AI analysis of why it performs as it does.
📉 Fatigue Detection
Use the normalized view (% of launch) to compare decay curves fairly. A creative above the top-performer benchmark line is genuinely resilient. One below the fatigued line needs intervention now.
🎯 Recommendations
Filter by KPI goal to see only the creatives relevant to your campaign type. The action (Scale / Monitor / Pause) is derived from status and KPI performance.
💡 ML Insights
Switch the model dropdown to see feature importance for your specific KPI. A high R² (e.g. 0.72) means the model reliably predicts performance; check MAE to understand the typical prediction error in absolute terms.
🔵 Clusters
Look at the cluster with the highest avg_perf. If your current creatives are all in the same cluster, you are likely over-indexing on a single creative concept — use the Portfolio Optimizer to diversify.
🧮 Portfolio Optimizer
Add your active creatives in Step 1. Move the slider toward Orthogonal to find creatives that test genuinely new territory. Use KPI targeting if your next campaign has a specific goal.
🔮 Predict Creative
Use this before commissioning new creative work. If the predicted score is Below Average, adjust the format, theme or features. Check the benchmark creatives shown — they are real examples in the same cluster with your KPI.
